requirements.requirement: Load the supplied HR LDIF into LDAP on node1 and retain the supplied records under /srv/legacy2/ldap-attribute-privacy.
requirements.summary: The supplied Morgan employee entry is present in LDAP on node1. The retained hr.ldif has the baseline SHA-256 hash, expected 201-byte size, and original contents, including employeeNumber HR-4815.

requirements.requirement: Allow the directory-reader identity to search employee names and mail addresses from node2 while preventing it from reading, searching by, or changing employeeNumber.
requirements.summary: Remote node2 searches as directory-reader return Morgan's cn and mail but omit employeeNumber. Filtering on employeeNumber returns zero entries, and an attempted employeeNumber modification is rejected with insufficient access.

requirements.requirement: Permit the HR administrator, and not ordinary reader or anonymous access, to read and change employeeNumber.
requirements.summary: The configured ACIs grant the HR administrator employee access while restricting the reader to public fields. The administrator directly reads, changes, verifies, restores, and re-verifies employeeNumber; the reader's change is denied. Final value is HR-4815.

requirements.requirement: Ensure anonymous users see no employee records.
requirements.summary: Anonymous employee searches from node2 return zero DNs before and after both node restarts and in the final check.

requirements.requirement: Provision dedicated demonstration credentials for the directory reader and HR administrator.
requirements.summary: Dedicated directory-reader and hr-admin LDAP entries were created. Their generated password files are stored in a root-only directory with mode 0600 and remain usable from node2 after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remain on RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8.x86_64. Installed LDAP components are EL9 packages, and package-health checks remain successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final behavior from node2. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: healthy pre-restart observations, restart acknowledgements, changed boot IDs consistent with lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, records, credentials, and access-control behavior are all captured. Operational hygiene is reduced by unnecessary persistent SSH-key handling, exposure of unused plaintext LDAP port 389, and abandoned temporary files.
limitations: The claim that only the HR administrator has employeeNumber access is supported by the explicit ACI configuration and direct reader, administrator, and anonymous tests, but evidence does not exhaustively probe every theoretically possible authenticated principal or the directory superuser.

Final lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /root/.ssh, so persistence and exact prior contents of the SSH key files are inferred from the successful write commands and absence of any recorded cleanup.
Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Functionality is healthy, package consistency is intact, and no failed services remain. However, several executor-caused hygiene issues remain. Port 389 was unnecessarily added to the persistent firewall alongside the actually used LDAPS port 636, retaining a plaintext LDAP exposure after reboot (cmd-22bdd0a6b45248dd, cmd-610691c413b04b09). SSH setup wrote the cluster private key on node2 even though node2 only needed to accept the incoming credential copy; no cleanup was recorded (cmd-50770ab6253b41fb). The analogous node1 command also touched its authorized_keys although only an outgoing private key was needed; whether it appended a new key cannot be established (cmd-1b3988b581cf4a72). Installation/template artifacts remained in /tmp: ds-template.inf and package log/PID files on node1, plus package log/PID files on node2 (cmd-06ed7d61815f46cf, cmd-dcd0d560dd924893, cmd-80ff8d40a33947d1). These were not reverted. The administrator's bounded test change to employeeNumber was fully restored and is not penalized.
